highlight.title: Leadership Dynamics in Teams: The Reciprocity of Shared and Empowering Leadership
highlight.summary: <cite index='1-4,1-5'>Recent theoretical developments indicate that leadership is a dynamic team process, valuing the contributions of leaders and followers alike. This pre-registered study investigates the reciprocal interplay between shared leadership and formal team leadership (i.e., empowering leadership).</cite> <cite index='1-17'>The research aims to better understand how a team of followers can influence their leader's behavior through their informal leadership attempts (i.e., shared leadership).</cite>

resources.title: To Lead Through Uncertainty, Unlearn Your Assumptions
resources.why_now: <cite index='21-2,21-3'>Leaders grow capacity by unlearning, which involves changing prior scripts, such as the assumptions that speed, reassurance, and control are necessary when making complex leadership decisions. It requires relearning ways of being that widen the room for reality and uncertainty.</cite>

resources.title: Psychological Safety and Emotional Intelligence: Building Resilient Teams in 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index='12-1,12-2'>To build psychological safety, enforce a "vulnerability ritual"—start meetings with 2-minute personal check-ins ("Share one win and one worry"). Research shows this increases speak-up behaviors by 40% within weeks.</cite> This provides immediately actionable tactics for leaders seeking measurable improvements.

resources.title: Leadership in Uncertainty: The Power of Timely Decisions
resources.why_now: <cite index='25-17,25-20'>Confidence develops as a result of making decisions, following through, and seeing outcomes. Not before. "Confidence is built through action," she maintains.</cite> This challenges the common misconception that leaders must feel ready before acting—crucial insight for uncertain times.

resources.title: How to rethink leadership in 2026, according to young leaders
resources.why_now: <cite index='27-4,27-6'>The defining skill for the next decade is not what leaders know, but how they make decisions when everything is in motion. Working at the intersection of political leadership development, civil society and large-scale private-sector projects, I learned that the defining skill for the next decade is not what leaders know, but how they make decisions when everything is in motion.</cite>

claude_take: The convergence of AI integration and psychological safety isn't coincidental—it's essential. <cite index='3-12,3-13'>DDI's research has identified five capabilities that give leaders the edge in an AI-driven world: Connection, Conscience, Creativity, Clarity, and Curiosity. Together, these 5Cs ensure that technology amplifies, rather than replaces, human leadership.</cite> The most successful leaders of 2026 will be those who master the paradox of leveraging AI's analytical power while deepening their capacity to create the human conditions where teams can think boldly and fail safely.
